headline: Choose between saving {cost.gap.f64.prod.monthly|usd_whole} monthly or keeping persona consistency on longer conversations.
lede: Switching to {arm:f64} saves {cost_per_1k.f64|usd_per_1k} against {cost_per_1k.prod|usd_per_1k} on {control.name}, while persona retention drops {contrast.f64.persona.delta|abs|pts} points ({contrast.f64.persona.interval|pts}). A product decision on acceptable loss at turn depths above five settles the choice.

slots.text: {arm:f64} cuts cost by {cost.gap.f64.prod.monthly|abs|usd_whole} each month, but drops Stays in character from {judged.persona.prod|pct} to {judged.persona.f64|pct}.
{arm:f64} is favored if saving at least {price.prod.f64.persona.per_point|usd} per point of Stays in character matters more than the drop.
Lean toward {arm:f64} because both standing guardrails hold and persona losses remain modest until conversation depth exceeds five turns.
A human review of turn depth above five to verify whether users tolerate the persona drift on long chats.

method.text: Multi-factor design comparing {control.name} against three challengers across {scoreboard.prod.cases} cases with eight repeats per case.
Stays in character evaluated with a calibrated judge rubric exhibiting {judged.persona.agreement} agreement across {judged.persona.calibration_ratings} human ratings.
Standing policy guardrails require at least {criteria.facts.threshold} on Music facts correct and {criteria.specul.threshold} on Declines to speculate.
Measured tokens multiplied by list price per 1,000 replies at an assumed monthly volume of {meta.volume_per_month} replies.
Differences reported with {family.level} confidence intervals on paired differences without multi-candidate correction.
Latency measured as end-to-end response time at median (p50) and p95 tail.

flag.text: The campaign declared no threshold for acceptable loss in Stays in character, leaving leadership to weigh cost against persona fidelity.
